questions.question: The following pie charts show the number of students studying in different departments of an institute during the academic years 2019 and 2020. What are the ratio of Commerce and Computer Science students taken together in 2019 to Engineering and Medical students taken together in 2020?
questions.solution:
Total students who took Commerce and Computer in 2019 = 2000 × (25 + 14)% ⇒ 2000 × 39% ⇒ 780

Total students who took Engineering and Medical in 2020 = 2400 × (12+ 10)% ⇒ 2400 × 22% ⇒ 528

Ratio = 780 : 528 ⇒ 65 : 44

questions.question: Study the given pie chart and answer the question that follows. The pie chart represents the percentage-wise distribution of the total number of Vanilla cakes and Chocolate cakes sold everyday in a week. The total number of cakes sold in a week = 10500. The ratio of the number of Vanilla cakes sold to the number of Chocolate cakes sold on Saturday is 4 ∶ 3, the selling price of one Vanilla cake is Rs. 8 and that of one Chocolate cake is Rs. 15, then the total amount earned (in Rs.) by selling all Vanilla cakes and Chocolate cakes on Saturday is:
questions.questionHtml:
Study the given pie chart and answer the question that follows.

The pie chart represents the percentage-wise distribution of the total number of Vanilla cakes and Chocolate cakes sold everyday in a week. The total number of cakes sold in a week = 10500.

The ratio of the number of Vanilla cakes sold to the number of Chocolate cakes sold on Saturday is 4 ∶ 3, the selling price of one Vanilla cake is Rs. 8 and that of one Chocolate cake is Rs. 15, then the total amount earned (in Rs.) by selling all Vanilla cakes and Chocolate cakes on Saturday is:
questions.solution:
The total number of cakes sold on Saturday = (16/100) × 10500 = 1680

The ratio of vanilla cakes sold to chocolate cakes sold on Saturday = 4 ∶ 3

The number of vanilla cake sold = (4/7) × 1680 = 960

The number of chocolate cake sold = 1680 - 960 = 720

The total sale = (960 × 8) + (720 × 15) = 7680 + 10800 = 18480.

questions.question: The given pie - diagram shows the expenditure incurred on the preparation of a book by a publisher, under various heads. Study the pie - diagram and answer the question that follows. Various Expenditure (in percentage) incurred in publishing a book The marked price of a book is 20% more than the CP. If the marked price of the book is 30, then what is the cost of paper used in a single copy of the book?
questions.questionHtml:
The given pie - diagram shows the expenditure incurred on the preparation of a book by a publisher, under various heads. Study the pie - diagram and answer the question that follows.

Various Expenditure (in percentage) incurred in publishing a book


The marked price of a book is 20% more than the CP. If the marked price of the book is 30, then what is the cost of paper used in a single copy of the book?
questions.solution:
Given:

Marked Price (MP) = ₹30

MP is 20% more than Cost Price (CP)

Percentage of expenditure on paper = 20%

Formula used:

MP = CP + 20% of CP

Cost of paper = 20% of CP

Calculation:

30 = CP + 0.2 × CP

⇒ 30 = 1.2 × CP

⇒ CP = 30 / 1.2

⇒ CP = 25

Cost of paper = 20% × 25

⇒ Cost of paper = 0.2 × 25

⇒ Cost of paper = 5

∴ The cost of paper used in a single copy of the book is ₹5.

What is the percentage increase or decrease in the number of students of Engineering in 2020 as compared to 2019? (correct to 2 decimal places)
questions.solution:
The number of Engineering students in 2019 = (13/100) × 2000 = 260

The number of Engineering students in 2020 = (12/100) × 2400 = 288

The number of Engineering students increases from 2019 to 2020 = 288 - 260 = 28.

The increase percentage = (28/260) × 100 = 10.769...% ≈ 10.77%.

⇒ 19%

questions.question: The given pie chart the percentage distribution of the expenditure incurred in publishing a book. Study the chart and answer the question that follows. If 2500 copies are published and the printing cost for them amounts to Rs. 160,000, then what should be the selling price of a book such that the publisher can earn a profit of 25%?
questions.questionHtml:
The given pie chart the percentage distribution of the expenditure incurred in publishing a book. Study the chart and answer the question that follows.

If 2500 copies are published and the printing cost for them amounts to Rs. 160,000, then what should be the selling price of a book such that the publisher can earn a profit of 25%?
questions.solution:
Given:

Number of copies published = 2500

Printing cost of 2500 published copies = ₹ 160000

Printing expenditure = 20%

Profit percentage on selling a book = 25%

Formula used:

Profit = Selling price – Cost price

Profit percentage = (Profit/Cost price) × 100

Calculation:

Printing cost of a book = 160000/2500 = 64

⇒ Total expenditure on a book = 64 × (100/20) = 320

⇒ Selling price of a book = 320 × {(100 + 25)/100} = 400

∴ The selling price of the book is ₹ 400.

questions.questionHtml:

The ratio of vanilla cakes sold to chocolate cakes sold on Friday = 4 ∶ 3.

questions.question: Study the given pie-charts and answer the question that follows. The pie-charts show the characteristics of foreign tourists visiting India during a given year. If in a given year, 2,50,000 tourists visited India and the age wise distribution of data applies to all the countries, then the number of Russian tourists who visited India during the year and were in the age group above 50 years is:
questions.questionHtml:
Study the given pie-charts and answer the question that follows.

If in a given year, 2,50,000 tourists visited India and the age wise distribution of data applies to all the countries, then the number of Russian tourists who visited India during the year and were in the age group above 50 years is:
questions.solution:
Given:

Total tourists = 2,50,000

Russian tourists = 15%

Tourists above 50 years = 10%

Formula used:

Russian tourists = Total tourists × Percentage of Russian tourists

Russian tourists above 50 years = Russian tourists × Percentage of tourists above 50 years

Calculation:

Russian tourists = 2,50,000 × 15%

⇒ Russian tourists = 37,500

Russian tourists above 50 years = 37,500 × 10%

⇒ Russian tourists above 50 years = 3,750

∴ The number of Russian tourists above 50 years is 3,750.

questions.question: The following pie-chart shows details of the per month expenditure of a family. Study the pie-chart carefully and answer the question that follows. The following pie-chart shows details of the per month expenditure of a family. Study the pie-chart carefully and answer the question that follows.

The expenditure on rent, medicines and electricity together is what percentage of the expenditure on groceries and education together?
questions.solution:
Given:

The percentages from the pie chart are:

Rent: 15%

Medicines: 10%

Electricity: 12%

Groceries: 20%

Education: 25%

Calculation:

Step 1: Add the expenditure percentages on rent, medicines, and electricity:

15% + 10% + 12% = 37%

Step 2: Add the expenditure percentages on groceries and education:

20% + 25% = 45%

Step 3: Calculate the required percentage:

Required percentage = (37 / 45) × 100

⇒ Required percentage = 82.22%

∴ The expenditure on rent, medicines, and electricity together is 82.22% of the expenditure on groceries and education together.

questions.question: The following chart shows the marks (in degrees) scored by a student in different subjects - English, Hindi, History, Economics, and Political Science - in an examination. The total marks obtained in the examination are 600. Observe the chart and answer the question. What is the difference between marks scored in History and marks scored in Hindi?
questions.questionHtml:
The following chart shows the marks (in degrees) scored by a student in different subjects - English, Hindi, History, Economics, and Political Science - in an examination. The total marks obtained in the examination are 600. Observe the chart and answer the question.

What is the difference between marks scored in History and marks scored in Hindi?
questions.solution:
Given :

A pie chart with central angles

Total marks obtained in the examination is 600

To find :

Difference Between marks scored in History and Hindi.

Concept used :

(the difference between the central angle/360°) × 600

Solution :

⇒ The central angle of marks scored in History = 70° 

⇒ The central angle of marks scored in Hindi = 55° 

⇒ Difference between the central angle = 70° - 55° 

⇒ Difference between the central angle = 15° 

⇒ Difference Between the marks scored in History and Hindi = (15°/360°) × 600

⇒ Difference Between the marks scored in History and Hindi = 25

∴ The difference Between the marks scored in History and Hindi is 25.

questions.question: The pie chart given below shows the percentage of employees in various departments of a company having a total workforce of 7200. Suppose the company plans to hire 324 more employees in the upcoming recruitment drive, of which 25% will be for the IT department, what would be the percentage increase in the number of employees in the IT department after the recruitment drive?
questions.questionHtml:
The pie chart given below shows the percentage of employees in various departments of a company having a total workforce of 7200.

Suppose the company plans to hire 324 more employees in the upcoming recruitment drive, of which 25% will be for the IT department, what would be the percentage increase in the number of employees in the IT department after the recruitment drive?
questions.solution:
Given:

Total Workforce = 7200

Total number of employees hired = 324

Percentage of hiring in IT department of of total hired = 25%

Calculation:

⇒ Number of IT employees before hiring = 30% of 7200 = (3/10) × 7200 = 2160

⇒ Increase in the number of IT employees after hiring = 25% × 324 = (1/4) × 324 = 81

∴  Percentage increase in the number of IT employee = (81/2160) × 100 = 3.75%

Hence, the correct answer is Option 1).

questions.question: The following pie charts show the number of students studying in different departments of an institute during the academic years 2019 and 2020. The total number of students was 2000 and 2400 in academic years 2019 and 2020, respectively. Students studying humanities in 2019 and 2020 taken together is what percentage of the total number of students studying during the two years taken together? (correct to 2 decimal places)
questions.questionHtml:
The following pie charts show the number of students studying in different departments of an institute during the academic years 2019 and 2020. The total number of students was 2000 and 2400 in academic years 2019 and 2020, respectively. 

Students studying humanities in 2019 and 2020 taken together is what percentage of the total number of students studying during the two years taken together? (correct to 2 decimal places)
questions.solution:
Number of students studying humanities in the year 2019 = 2000 × (21/100) ⇒ 420

Number of students studying humanities in the year 2020 = 2400 × (19/100) ⇒ 456

Total number of students studying humanities in the year 2019 and 2020 = 420 + 456 ⇒ 876

Percentage of students studying humanities in the year 2019 and 2020 = [876/(2000 + 2400)] × 100

⇒ [876/4400] × 100 ⇒ 876/44 ⇒ 19.909 ≈ 19.91

questions.questionHtml:
Study the given pie chart and answer the question that follow.

The pie charts represents the distribution of candidates who were enrolled for Bank Clerical Examination Fig(i) and the candidates (out of those enrolled) who passed the examination Fig(ii) in five different institutions P, Q, R, S and T.

(I) total number of candidates enrolled in five different institutes = 5500

(II) Total number of candidates who passed the examination from five institutes = 3300

 

The percentage of the candidates who passed to the number of candidates enrolled for institutes P and T together is:
questions.solution:
Calculation:

The number of candidates enrolled for institutes P and T together = (20 + 20)% = 40%

Total number of candidates enrolled in five different institutes = 5500

The number of candidates enrolled for institutes P and T together

⇒ (40% of 5500)

⇒ (40/100 × 5500)

⇒ 2200

Now,

The number of candidates passed from institutes P and T together = (18 + 16)% = 34%

Total number of candidates who passed the examination from five institutes = 3300

The number of candidates passed from institutes P and T together 

⇒ (34% of 3300)

⇒ (34/100 × 3300)

⇒ 1122

Now,

The percentage of the candidates who passed to the number of candidates enrolled for institutes P and T together 

⇒ (1122/2200 × 100)%

⇒ (1122/22)%

⇒ 51%

∴ The required percentage is 51%

questions.question: The given pie charts represent the popularity of ice-cream flavours in the years 2005 and 2015. If a percentage point shift results in annual additional sales of Rs. 5,000. how much (in Rs.) did the combined annual strawberry and butterscotch sales increase from 2005 to 2015 ?

The given pie charts represent the popularity of ice-cream flavours in the years 2005 and 2015.

 

If a percentage point shift results in annual additional sales of Rs. 5,000. how much (in Rs.) did the combined annual strawberry and butterscotch sales increase from 2005 to 2015 ?
questions.solution:
Given:

1% = Rs. 5000

In 2005,

Strawberry = 18.90%, Butterscotch = 10.80%

In 2015,

Strawberry = 20.50%, Butterscotch = 16.60%

Calculation:

Total sales in 2005

⇒ 18.90 + 10.80

⇒ 29.70%

Total sales in 2015

⇒ 20.50 + 16.60

⇒ 37.10%

Percentage Increase

⇒ 37.10 - 29.70

⇒ 7.4%

⇒ 7.4 × 5000

⇒ 37000

∴ The percentage increase from 2005 to 2015 is Rs. 37000.

questions.question: Study the given pie chart and answer the question that follows. The pie chart shows the percentage-wise distribution of teachers who teach six different subjects. If three-eighth of the teachers who teach Chemistry are females, then the number of male Chemistry teachers is what percentage of the total number of teachers who teach Biology?
questions.solution:
Total number of Chemistry teachers = 1600 × (18/100) = 288

Number of female Chemistry teachers = 288 × (3/8) = 108

Male Chemistry teacher = 288 - 108 = 180

Total number of Biology teachers = 1600 × (15/100) = 240

Required % = (180/240) × 100 = 75
